patient.key: Foul-smelling diarrhea worsening to Day 3 + E. coli on stool culture sensitive to cipro

sequence.what: 29M, abdominal pain and diarrhea for 8 days, office visit
sequence.decision: Acute diarrhea in a young adult â€” 8 days is subacute, not chronic. Start with history and broad workup.

sequence.what: T 37.5, HR 98, BP 129/87, RR 16, BMI 27.8 â€” mild tachycardia, otherwise stable
sequence.decision: Mildly tachycardic but not in distress. Afebrile.

sequence.what: Crampy abdominal pain, frequent loose stools, no blood/melena. Foul-smelling. Uses multivitamin. Single, no children. Smokes 1/2 PPD. Drinks socially. Marketing firm.
sequence.decision: No red flags in PMH. Social: smoker. Foul-smelling = consider infectious.

sequence.what: Abdomen: mild tenderness only. Rectal: no occult blood, no masses, normal. Rest full exam normal.
sequence.decision: No perianal involvement, no blood â€” rules out IBD. Non-inflammatory diarrhea pattern.

sequence.status: Placed diagnostic labs. Tdap ordered early â€” should have waited for after treatment.

sequence.result: CBC: WBC 8.5K, Hgb 15.0 â€” all normal. CMP: BUN 14, Cr 1.0, LFTs normal, calcium normal. No dehydration, no organ dysfunction.
sequence.decision: Normal labs rule out severe dehydration and organ failure. ESR = 0 mm/hr â€” confirms non-inflammatory.

sequence.result: C. diff PCR negative. C. diff toxin negative.

sequence.decision: Patient is decompensating despite supportive care. Need to broaden stool studies.

sequence.result: E. coli grown â€” resistant to cephalosporins, sensitive to ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin, azithromycin
sequence.decision: Enteropathogenic E. coli is the culprit. Cipro or azithromycin for treatment.

sequence.what: Vomiting frequently, severe abdominal pain, worsening diarrhea, dizzy.
sequence.decision: Patient is now clinically worsening â€” switch from oral to IV antibiotics immediately.
Giardia ruled out. E. coli remains the diagnosis.

sequence.status: Switched to IV ciprofloxacin after Giardia negative. Metronidazole stopped being needed once Giardia was ruled out.

missed.why: The mucosal protein released under stress. ESR = 0 doesn't suffice alone â€” calprotectin + ESR together confirm non-inflammatory etiology. Stool calprotectin is more specific for colonic inflammation than serum ESR.
Independent inflammatory marker, not the same as ESR. ESR = 0 + low CRP = locked non-inflammatory diagnosis. Ordered verbally but never placed.
You recognized this yourself â€” Hepatitis A can present with acute diarrhea and abdominal pain. LFTs were normal so it's unlikely, but it's an expected CCS order for acute diarrhea workup.
1/2 PPD smoker. Free point in every CCS case with a smoker. Always order regardless of diagnosis.
Antibiotic resistance prevention. Every antibiotic case needs this.

timingErrors.fix: Preventive care should be ordered AFTER the acute problem is treated, not in the initial order stack. Tdap is for 'later safe keeping' â€” literally order it at the end.

timingErrors.error: One negative patient update before correct treatment
timingErrors.fix: Patient worsened on Day 3 before IV cipro started. With E. coli on culture at Day 2, treatment should have started immediately upon seeing the sensitivity report.

mechanismsForImage.title: Healthy Gut â€” E. coli Invasion
mechanismsForImage.concept: Enteropathogenic E. coli bacteria attaching to intestinal epithelium, disrupting microvilli

mechanismsForImage.title: Toxin Secretion
mechanismsForImage.concept: E. coli secreting enterotoxins that pump chloride into the lumen, dragging water by osmosis

mechanismsForImage.title: Secretory Diarrhea
mechanismsForImage.concept: Water flooding the intestinal lumen, foul-smelling liquid stool, villi overwhelmed

mechanismsForImage.title: Non-Inflammatory Pattern
mechanismsForImage.concept: ESR = 0, no blood, no fever â€” the mucosa is intact, no WBC infiltration. Pure secretory diarrhea.

mechanismsForImage.title: Dehydration Cascade
mechanismsForImage.concept: Patient vomiting, dizzy, tachycardic â€” volume depletion without inflammation

mechanismsForImage.title: Culture + Sensitivity
mechanismsForImage.concept: E. coli colonies on agar plate with antibiotic discs â€” cephalosporins show no zone (resistant), ciprofloxacin shows wide zone (sensitive)

mechanismsForImage.title: Ciprofloxacin Mechanism
mechanismsForImage.concept: Fluoroquinolone molecule binding bacterial DNA gyrase, preventing DNA replication â€” the bacteria stop dividing

mechanismsForImage.title: Giardia Negative Contrast
mechanismsForImage.concept: Giardia antigen test strip showing negative (single control line only) â€” the parasite was ruled out, narrowing to E. coli

mechanismsForImage.title: Recovery
mechanismsForImage.concept: IV fluids repleting the depleted intravascular volume, cipro clearing the E. coli, intestinal epithelium regenerating

ordersPlaced: Polymerase chain reaction, clostridium difficile, stool
